newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end mixed, off early lows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end mixed, off early lows.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Monday, but off early lows in line with the yen's retreat against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from three yen per gram lower to one yen firmer. Most-active benchmark February was off one yen at 1,400 yen.
Activity was lacklustre. Gold futures started lower as long-liquidation by private investors emerged from the outset following a dip in bullion prices, the traders said.
"Except for selling in the morning, trade was quiet, moving in line with the currency market," one trader said.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted weaker at $346.30/60 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $346.60/347.10 in New York on Friday.

Traders said sentiment in the gold bullion market remained bearish with no bullish factors in sight. "Spot gold has more room to slip, but support at around $343 levels may be maintained on physical demand in Asia," an official of a bullion house said.
Platinum and palladium futures also ended mixed in directionless trade amid uncertainty over the expected resumption of Russian exports to Japan.

Palladium short-term lease rates, the cost of borrowing the metal remained at extremely high levels of 10 to 15 percent on Monday, up from about three percent earlier this year, reflecting a tightening in the spot market, the traders said.
Traders said the high lease rates are likely to continue unless Russia resumes the metal sales in the spot market.

Benchmark February palladium was down seven yen per gram at 606 yen. Benchmark February platinum was off two yen per gram at 1,475 yen. Benchmark February silver was down 2.3 yen per 10 grams at 193.7 yen.
